summary: Swami Vivekananda was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University (~1879–1880), Scottish Church College (~1881–1884), and the University of Calcutta (~1879–1884), and was a student of Ramakrishna (~1881–1886).
Sydney Frank Markham worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Wadham College (~1920–1923), he served as Secretary and then President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).

Syed Ali Bilgrami was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, Royal School of Mines (~1876–1879), Lucknow, and London, he served in the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and as Cambridge's Reader in Marathi (1901).

Syed Ameer Ali worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (~1867–1869), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta (~1877–1881).

Syed Hasan Askari was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College (~1918–1922), and Patna University (~1922–1924), later serving as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. He served as Principal at Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, both attested in 1932.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) under Marie-Claude Porcher and holds a post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Iranian/Central Asian specialist. He studied under Abel Bergaigne at the Sorbonne (~1881–1888) and held posts at the EPHE, University of Paris, Collège de France (1890–1935), and Maison Franco-Japonaise.

Sylvie Hureau specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Sze-bong Tso specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, the University of Göttingen (1815–1818), and under Tibetan teachers Sangye Phuntsok and Kunga Cholek Dorje, later serving as Librarian at The Asiatic Society.
Søren Sørensen was an Indologist. He held teaching posts at the Herlufsholm School (1876–1878) and at the University of Copenhagen (~1887–1902).
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He founded Path Press and served as an editor for the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano was a scholar who pursued studies under Narada Maha Thera, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Nyanaponika Thera.

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied as a pupil under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951).

T. Ganapati Sastri was an Indologist who earned a PhD from the University of Tübingen (~1924). He served as Curator of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library and Editor of the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series (~1908–1926).

T. Griffith Foulk specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1979–1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez, later teaching there (~1987–1995) and holding professorships at Sarah Lawrence College (~1995–2012).
T. K. V. Desikachar worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1961–1989) and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. N. Ramachandran worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Archæologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1928–1934), and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Madras studying under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked at the Adyar Library (~1927–1930) and was Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Madras (1933).
